scope.description: A node in the captured module constructed by NewRaft over stores that already hold a snapshot which the same node produced, observed before any election or leader contact.
assumptions: the stored snapshot is one the node itself took after committing and applying through its index
the restarted node's last index is the snapshot index, so no legal commit index exceeds it
excluded: the correctness of the snapshot payload itself, which the check does not inspect
the configuration carried by the snapshot
behaviour after an election or a leader contact has advanced the value
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: No target file is modified; the harness adds one external test file to the captured package and uses only public APIs (NewRaft, BootstrapCluster, Apply, Barrier, Snapshot, Shutdown, CommitIndex, AppliedIndex, LastIndex, Stats, State).
The snapshot is produced by the node itself through the public Snapshot API, so the restored index is an index that node had committed and applied and had published as such.
The same LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore instances are reused across the restart, so the second construction restores the state the first one left rather than a fixture.
The restarted instance's election timers are long only so that nothing campaigns between construction and the read; the observation is taken immediately after NewRaft returns.

plan_uncertainties: The observation is taken immediately after construction, so it does not measure how long the value stays low before a leader contacts the node or an election occurs; a single-voter configuration would advance it as soon as the node campaigns.
The observable is an index value rather than a state transition, so the check reports what the node published rather than a downstream consequence for a caller.
The restart keeps the log entries the snapshot covers, because TrailingLogs is left large; a configuration that compacted them away is not exercised.
grounding_unresolved: whether the published value is intentionally limited to the leader's last advertised commit index, which no source states
whether any consumer depends on the value on a restarted node
whether the omission is deliberate, i.e. whether the published commit index is intended to mean only the value the leader last advertised
whether the intended repair advances the commit index during the restore or derives the published value from the last snapshot index
whether a leader election immediately after the restart advances the value before a caller could read it, which this prefix deliberately does not produce
